Use the reading *Roads that held an empire*. The paragraph numbers (¶) tell you where to look.

## A. Vocabulary hunt

Find the word that matches the clue and write it in the Word box.

::: vocab-hunt
- ¶1 | _n._ a group of lands ruled by one leader | empire
- ¶1 | _n._ people who fight in an army | soldiers
- ¶2 | _n._ small stones | gravel
- ¶2 | _v._ to let water flow away | drain
- ¶3 | _n._ people who buy and sell things | merchants
- ¶4 | _n._ a channel or bridge that carries water | aqueduct
- ¶4 | _n._ the force that pulls things down | gravity
- ¶5 | _n._ curved shapes that hold up a bridge | arches
:::

## B. Reading recall

Answer each question in a complete sentence.

::: recall
- Why did Rome need roads? | To move soldiers, letters and food quickly around the empire.
- Why was the top of the road curved? | So rain ran off to the sides and the road stayed dry.
- How did water move along an aqueduct without pumps? | Gravity: the channel sloped gently downhill.
:::

## C. Building a road

Number the steps from 1 to 4 in the order the builders did them.

::: {.sequence order="3,1,4,2"}
- Lay flat paving stones on top.
- Dig a deep trench.
- Make the top curved so rain runs off.
- Fill the bottom with large stones.
:::

{{< pagebreak >}}

## D. Two-step equations

Solve each one. Show every step in the box.

::: {.problems cols="2"}
- $3x + 5 = 20$ | 5 | 3x = 15, so x = 5
- $2x - 7 = 9$ | 8 | 2x = 16, so x = 8
- $x / 4 + 3 = 8$ | 20 | x/4 = 5, so x = 20
- $5x + 2 = 3x + 10$ | 4 | 2x = 8, so x = 4
:::
